_comment: digperiphs (I2CT) proof configuration: the Castalia defaults with the I2CT0 hardware-autonomous I2C TARGET (slave) instantiated in the MUTEX page sub-slot 10 (peripherals.i2ctarget=true, @0x6A00). I2CT0 adds NO new pins -- it shares the I2C0 SDA0/SCL0 pad planes via an open-drain wired-AND DIR merge (target clock stretching + ACK/data driving; the merge is a separate shared-RTL edit). The whole target engine (7-bit address match + mask + general call, byte-at-a-time RX/TX with ready/empty status, hardware clock stretching, START/STOP/repeated-START/NACK framing flags, stuck-SCL watchdog, two combined IRQs) rides the free-running MCLK (D4-clean: 2-FF SDA/SCL sync, no pad-clocked processes), so the SYS_CLK_CR=0 footgun does NOT bind I2CT0 itself. Enabling it extends the IRQ source list per the A5 GLOBAL VECTOR RULE from 114 to 124: vectors 114/115/116/117/118/119 backfill as IRQB_RSVD (RTC/PWM/OW/DMA off), 120/121 backfill as IRQB_RSVD120/121 (always-False DP-SG placeholders -- npu-thinkdone/TRNG, not yet landed), 122 = I2CT0_AE (address/error), 123 = I2CT0_DATA (tx-ready/rx-full); NUM_EN_WORDS stays 4 (124 <= 128). MmrAddrI2CT0 + RegSlotI2CT0* appear in MemoryMap.vhd only when the knob is on. Everything else is default. Prove with: make verify CONFIG=config/castalia_i2ctarget.json
